title: Lifting smoothing traits to etale charts and detecting density
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $\mathcal F$ be a Deligne--Mumford stack on $k$-schemes, and let $\mathcal U\subset\mathcal F$ be an open full substack. Stack, scheme atlas, 2-fibre product and geometric point have the conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-weil-geometric-point]; open means that pullback along every scheme-valued object is represented by an open subscheme. Suppose that for every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and every object $x\in\mathcal F(\Omega)$ there is an object $\xi\in\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega[[t]])$, with an isomorphism $\xi|_{t=0}\simeq x$ and with $\xi|_{\operatorname{Spec}\Omega((t))}$ in $\mathcal U$. The rings are the one-variable formal power-series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] and its localization obtained by inverting $t$. For any representable etale morphism $a:V\to\mathcal F$ from a $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-etale-morphism], any geometric point $v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$, and any such $\xi$ equipped with $\xi|_{t=0}\simeq a(v)$, there is a morphism $\widetilde v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega[[t]]\to V$ restricting to $v$, together with a 2-isomorphism $a\widetilde v\simeq\xi$ restricting to that prescribed isomorphism. Consequently the open subscheme $V\times_{\mathcal F}\mathcal U$ is dense in $V$ (its closure in the underlying topological space is all of $V$). No surjectivity of $a$, smoothness of $\mathcal F/k$, or finite-type hypothesis on $V/k$ is required.

proof.text: Put $R=\Omega[[t]]$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$, and let $i:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ be constant-coefficient reduction. The power-series local-ring and quotient lemmas identify the maximal ideal with $(t)$ and the residue map with $R\twoheadrightarrow\Omega$. The variables-completeness lemma makes $R$ $(t)$-adically complete; the complete-pair lemma therefore makes $(R,(t))$ henselian. Thus $R$ is a henselian local ring with the specified residue map. This uses no property of the stack.

source.place: Tag 0ALJ (lemma-complete-henselian); power-series inputs in algebra.tex, Remark 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary), specialized to one variable over a field.

proof.text: Form $E=T\times_{\mathcal F}V$. Representability of $a$ makes this an algebraic space and etale base change makes $p:E\to T$ etale. The prescribed special-fibre isomorphism defines a point $e:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to E$ over $i$: its components are $i$, $v$, and that isomorphism (inverted if the 2-fibre-product convention requires it). Choose an etale surjective scheme atlas $w:W\to E$. Its pullback $P=W\times_E\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is a scheme etale and surjective over $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, hence nonempty. Etale implies weakly etale, so the algebraically-closed-field section lemma gives $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to P$. Its projection is a lift $z:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to W$ of the actual point $e$. Composition in the chartwise etale calculus makes $q=pw:W\to T$ etale.

proof.text: Apply affine pointed-neighbourhood shrinking to the etale scheme map $q$ and $z$, with the whole of $W$ as the open neighbourhood. Obtain $j:\operatorname{Spec}B\hookrightarrow W$ and $z_0:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $jz_0=z$ and $qj$ etale. Write $\alpha:R\to B$ for $qj$ and $\theta:B\to\Omega$ for $z_0$. The equation $qjz_0=i$ is $\theta\alpha=\epsilon$, where $\epsilon:R\twoheadrightarrow\Omega$ is constant coefficient. Apply the henselian ring lifting lemma with base ring $R$, target henselian local ring $S=R$, base map $\beta=1_R$, field $K=\Omega$, and this $\epsilon,\theta$. It yields $f:B\to R$ with $f\alpha=1_R$ and $\epsilon f=\theta$. Hence $s=j\operatorname{Spec}f:T\to W$ satisfies $qs=1_T$ and $si=z$, as equalities of scheme morphisms.

source.place: Tag 08HQ (lemma-map-into-henselian), with S=R; affine shrinking: etale-cohomology.tex 04HX (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring), affine-neighbourhood paragraph.

proof.text: The section $ws:T\to E$ over $T$, composed with $E\to V$, gives $\widetilde v$. Unwinding the 2-fibre product gives a 2-isomorphism $a\widetilde v\simeq\xi$. Because $wsi=wz=e$, its restriction at $i$ is the originally prescribed triple, not merely a point with the same image. More explicitly, the equivalence between $E$ and the discrete fibred groupoid of its representing algebraic space supplies an isomorphism between this restricted triple and $(i,v,\phi)$. Since schemes as fibred groupoids have only identity arrows, its two scheme components are identities; the compatibility equation for an arrow of the 2-fibre product is exactly equality of the restricted 2-isomorphism with $\phi$. Thus $\widetilde v i=v$ and the required framing is preserved.

proof.text: The power-series domain lemma gives that $(0)$ is prime in $R$. It is contained in $(t)$, so the point $(t)$ lies in the closure of the singleton $(0)$: every basic open $D(h)$ containing $(t)$ has $h\notin(t)$, hence $h\ne0$, and contains $(0)$. Moreover every nonzero series is $t^n u$ for a unit $u$: take its least nonzero coefficient and use the unit criterion of the power-series local-ring lemma. Consequently $R[1/t]=\Omega((t))$ is a field and its spectrum maps to $(0)$. Under the continuous scheme map $\widetilde v$, the image of this generic point therefore specializes to the image of $v$. The 2-isomorphism just constructed and fullness of the open substack show that this generic point maps into $V\times_{\mathcal F}\mathcal U$.

source.place: Tag 0E86 (lemma-smooth-dense), final sentences: the generic point specializes to the closed point.

proof.text: For every underlying point $y\in V$, choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(y)$ and the corresponding geometric point $v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$. The residue-field description of geometric points shows its image is $y$; the structural field maps make $\Omega$ an extension of $k$. Apply the assumed trait existence to $a(v)$ and then steps 1--5 to its prescribed special identification. They put $y$ in the closure of $V\times_{\mathcal F}\mathcal U$. This holds for every $y$, so that closure is all of $V$. Its openness is precisely the stipulated scheme-test definition of the open substack. When $V$ is empty the same conclusion holds vacuously. Neither this argument nor the lifting construction uses surjectivity of $a$, smoothness of $\mathcal F$, or finite type over $k$.
